competition_official.name: GEMS Prize Challenge main page
facts: End date Dec 3, 2026 11:59 p.m. UTC
Total prize pool $300,000
Initial round: top 5 on private test set, $10,000 each
Final round: $100k/$70k/$40k/$25k/$15k on expanded label set
Eligibility: individuals must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents; team captain U.S. citizen/PR
Sponsor: DOE Office of Geothermal with support from National Lab of the Rockies (NLR)
Contact: gemsprize@nlr.gov
3 key rules highlighted: eligibility, use of test data, use of external data

competition_official.name: Problem description page
facts: Task: predict geological faults in GeoDAWN region
Metric: distance-weighted Tversky index, triangular kernel k(d)=max(1-d/300m,0), alpha=0.2 (FP), beta=0.8 (FN)
Submission: single-layer float32 GeoTIFF, [0,1], EPSG:32611, 100m, same bounds as training data, NaN outside

training_features.tif bands: surface conductivity + depth to conductive base; detrended elevation + slope; dilatation/shear strain/second invariant of strain rate; isostatic gravity anomaly + slope; RTP magnetic anomaly, TMI, vertical+horizontal slope of TMI, top-of-crustal magnetic source depth; earthquake density
1m_DEM_links.csv provided for 1m DEM
Labels from USGS quaternary fault maps and INGENIOUS, vector + raster
External data allowed with license permitting use and sharing with sponsor

competition_official.name: About page
facts: GeoDAWN = USGS+DOE airborne magnetic/radiometric over N/W Nevada and E California, under EarthMRI with DOE Office of Geothermal support
Coordinated 3DEP airborne lidar
Fault detection background and methods
Recommended reading: Matteo et al 2021 (doi:10.1029/2020JB021269) and Hermant et al 2025 (Stanford SGW)

competition_official.name: Official rules PDF (fy26osti 96647, September 2026)
facts: Governed by 15 U.S.C. 3719; not a procurement or grant
1.1: two phases; Phase 1 $50,000 split equally among top 5 on private test set; Phase 2 $250,000 = $100k/$70k/$40k/$25k/$15k on updated label set

1.3: individual competitors must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents; team captains U.S. citizen/PR; FFRDC researchers may compete individually (honorable mention only, no cash); federal employees and DOE-affiliated persons ineligible; FCOC/MFTRP restrictions
1.4: prize goals including commercialization intent statement
3.2: register on DrivenData; single GeoTIFF single raster layer 100m for entire GeoDAWN area; up to three submissions per week; must indicate generative-AI use in narrative

3.3: training labels contain existing fault data obtained from INGENIOUS project Great Basin Regional Dataset Compilation (footnote 4: Ayling et al. 2022, doi:10.15121/1881483); features footnote 3: Glen & Earney 2024 GeoDAWN doi:10.5066/P93LGLVQ
3.4: up to 3 submissions/week; choose exactly ONE final submission
3.5: one submission scored across both prize rounds; complete code assets + documentation consistent with DrivenData Winning Model Documentation Template
3.6.1: public/private split of ground truth; public shown on leaderboard
3.6.2: choose single submission without knowledge of private scores
3.6.5: winner notification ~60 days after close
A.1: submit by 5:00 p.m. ET on deadline; English; certification under penalty of perjury
A.2: ACH + IRS W-9 within 30 days of notice

competition_official.name: Reference solution (github drivendataorg/gems-prize-reference-solution)
facts: Author: John Lipor (Portland State)
Notebook: unet-mc-cv-reference-solution.ipynb
Uses data/numeric_features.tif and data/labels.tif
segmentation_models_pytorch U-Net; MC=5 splits; patch_size=128; test_proportion=0.5; batch 32; epochs 5; init_lr 1e-4; Tversky alpha 0.2 beta 0.8
patchify helpers adapted from patchify.py (MIT)
Output: predicted_faults_example.tif with CRS/transform from labels
